post.summary: A challenge for key attestation, valid 10 minutes. Android: generate the key with setAttestationChallenge(challenge as ASCII bytes), then add attestation {format:"android-key", challenge, x5c[]} to the enrollment request. iOS: attestKey with clientDataHash SHA-256("<challenge>.<JWK thumbprint of the enrolled key>") and add {format:"apple-appattest", challenge, app_id, key_id, object}. TPM 2.0 (Windows): TPM2_Certify the TPM-resident P-256 key with the AIK and qualifyingData SHA-256("<challenge>.<JWK thumbprint>"), and add {format:"tpm", challenge, alg, x5c[], sig, cert_info, pub_area}. TPM 2.0 without a Microsoft AIK certificate (Linux): see POST /api/v1/enrollments/tpm-activation. Free; stateless.

200.description: Success. Every JSON response includes cost_microdollars.

post.summary: TPM 2.0 attestation by EK credential activation, step 1, for TPMs whose attestation key (AK) has no Microsoft certificate. Send {challenge, ek_certificate (the TPM's RSA-2048 EK certificate, DER base64; NV index 0x01c00002), ek_chain[] (optional CA certificates up to the manufacturer's), ak_pub_area (the restricted signing AK, TPM2B_PUBLIC or TPMT_PUBLIC), pub_area (the TPM-resident P-256 device key), cert_info (TPMS_ATTEST from TPM2_Certify of the device key by the AK), sig (TPMT_SIGNATURE)}. Answers a secret wrapped for that TPM (id_object, encrypted_secret, and credential_blob in tpm2_activatecredential's file format) and an activation token valid 10 minutes. Unwrap with TPM2_ActivateCredential and add attestation {format:"tpm-ek", challenge, activation, secret (base64)} to the enrollment request. Free; stateless.
